stromatoporoid (mainly “ Aculatosproma ”) bindstones are composed of a combination of skeletal and microbial frameworks, which are repeatedly accumulated at each observation scale, and that the accumulation patterns reflect the interrelationships between skeletal frameworks and microbialites within their habitable range.

the repeated accumulation patterns of stromatoporoids and microbialites in a bioherm of Lower Devonian age are indicative of antagonistic interactions between skeletal organisms, and between skeletal organisms (mainly stromatoporoids) and microbes.

the accumulation patterns of the Lower Devoniant Stromatoporoid Bindstones are marked by a succession from laminar stromatopoids to microbialites and then to laminar stromatoproiods, and this succession reflects differences in the tolerences of the organisms responsible and corresponds to fluctuating environments.

the stromatoporoids were the primary framework-builders and the microbialites were secondary, but the stromatoporoidal framework was not the only factor in controlling the microbialite accumulation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the repeated accumulation patterns are a result of the competitive interactions among the three organisms: 1) stromatoporoids; 2) stromatoporoid-associated microbes; 3) stromatoporoidal cryptic spaces.

repeated accumulations of stromatoporoids and microbialites at each scale are the result of the competitive superiority of the skeletal framework, and of the tolerance of the framework to deteriorating conditions.

stromatoporoid frameworks were the main contributors to biohermal limestones of Lower Devonian age, but the framework-building organisms themselves were not always the dominant organisms within their habitable range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stromatoporoid–microbe interrelationships are important for understanding the evolution of stromatoporoids and their ecological roles in the Palaeozoic.

the repeated appearance of microbialites and the recurrence of skeletal organisms at each observation level reflect a complex interplay of skeletal frameworks and microbialites, and that these accumulation patterns provide invaluable information about the interactions between skeletal frameworks, microbialites, and microenvironments.
